caption: N=1 baseline: a lever on the back of a sticky piston.

Pushes a block out two cells from a one-block-wide wall: the lever's piston shoves a strip of three slime blocks forward, and a second sticky piston riding on that strip pushes the block one step further; switching off pulls the strip back and the riding piston grabs the block home. How it works: an observer hanging under the strip blinks 2 ticks after every move and fires the riding piston (the lever's piston ignores it, a piston is never powered through its own face); the riding piston's short pulse leaves the block on the strip's front slime, which carries it back on the way home.
N=2, slime + observer, 7 blocks: the observer beside S1 powers it (B stands on it).

Pushes a block out two cells with no slime: two sticky pistons in a line; flipping the lever makes the back piston throw the front piston and the block forward, then the lever holds the front piston out; switching off brings them back one at a time. How it works: an observer next to the lever blinks on every flip and pulses the back piston (through the stone beside it); on the way back the front piston lets go, the back piston grabs it home, and a second observer carried along fires as it lands, so the front piston reaches out and grabs the block home.

N=2, slime-free, 7 blocks: an observer watching the input gives a 2 gt pulse on BOTH edges to A (through the stone beside it) and to a second sticky piston that carries an observer. On: A pushes B + payload and spits them (B lands next to the input, which holds it extended: the payload goes one more cell). Off: B retracts (payload back one), A's pulse reach-pulls B home, and the carried observer, pulled home too, fires on landing into B (variant 2: where it sits), whose 2 gt pulse reach-pulls the payload home. The lever hangs on the input observer.

A 2-piston extender you can flip back at any time (7 blocks, 3x5x1, one block thick): it lifts a sand block 2 cells (out in 8 gt, back in 12 gt), and turning the lever off or on again early never strands a block. How it works: the lever drives a small piston beside the column and, through the cell above it, the upper piston. An observer watching the small piston's head fires once at each lever flip and gives the sticky piston at the bottom a short pulse: when the upper piston is home, the pulse lifts it and the sand one cell and leaves them there, and the upper piston, still powered by the lever, pushes the sand one more; when the upper piston is up, the pulse pulls it back down, and the sand falls home. Found by `mctas circuit pext anneal --flip-soft` from pext-n2-sand6 (pext).
